messages.content: I'd like to work through our longer vacation now. We are considering Kauai for seven nights, either June 3-10 or June 10-17, 2028. Please compare the whole trip for two people, not just the room rates.

I can compare both weeks on the same basis. Are you still considering the two beachfront properties you mentioned, Koloa Bay Resort and Hanalei Shore Hotel, and should I include a rental car from arrival through departure?

Yes. One car for the entire stay. Include airfare from San Francisco, seven room nights, all hotel taxes and mandatory charges, parking, and breakfast for both of us. We do not need activities or inter-island flights.

I found current nonstop air and flexible hotel pricing for both weeks. The June 3 week has the lower room rates, but nonstop airfare is $728 per person round trip. June 10 has airfare at $566 per person, although oceanfront inventory is tighter. I am checking the hotel charges line by line before totaling the combinations.
Good. Also show the flight times. A low total is not useful if we lose most of the first or last day.

For June 3-10, the nonstop leaves SFO at 8:20 a.m. and reaches LIH at 11:14 a.m. The return leaves LIH at 1:05 p.m. and reaches SFO at 9:18 p.m. For June 10-17, the outbound leaves at 9:10 a.m. and arrives at 12:04 p.m.; the return has the same 1:05-9:18 p.m. schedule. Both allow a useful arrival afternoon, though the first week gains about 50 minutes.
What did you find at Koloa Bay?

Koloa Bay includes daily breakfast for two and self-parking. For June 3-10, an ocean-view king is $515 per night: $3,605 room, $641.69 tax, and no separate mandatory resort or parking charge, for $4,246.69 lodging total. For June 10-17, the remaining oceanfront king is $569 per night: $3,983 room plus $708.97 tax, totaling $4,691.97. Only two rooms in that category are showing for the second week.
And Hanalei Shore? Its displayed room price looked substantially lower.

Its headline rate is lower, but the additions change the comparison. June 3-10 has a partial-ocean-view king at $455 nightly: $3,185 room, $566.93 room tax, $453.25 in mandatory resort charges including tax, $307.86 for self-parking including tax, and an estimated $378 for breakfast for two across seven mornings. That makes the lodging portion $4,891.04.
Use breakfast prices that are actually realistic there, including tax and tip. I do not want a bare menu subtotal.

The $378 estimate does that. It uses $54 per day for two, based on the current breakfast pricing with tax and an 18% tip. For June 10-17, the deluxe ocean-view king is $475 nightly. The breakdown is $3,325 room, $591.85 tax, $453.25 resort charges, $307.86 parking, and $378 breakfast, for $5,055.96 in lodging and breakfast.
Now add the cars and airfare. Please put all four complete totals in one comparison.

The full-stay midsize rental is $612.40 including taxes and facility fees for June 3-10, and $548.20 for June 10-17. With airfare for two, the complete totals are: June 3 Koloa Bay, $1,456 air + $4,246.69 lodging + $612.40 car = $6,315.09; June 3 Hanalei Shore, $1,456 + $4,891.04 + $612.40 = $6,959.44; June 10 Koloa Bay, $1,132 + $4,691.97 + $548.20 = $6,372.17; June 10 Hanalei Shore, $1,132 + $5,055.96 + $548.20 = $6,736.16.
So the least expensive combination is the earlier week, but only by about sixty dollars compared with Koloa Bay in the later week. Is that right?

Yes. June 3 at Koloa Bay is $57.08 less than June 10 at Koloa Bay. The later week saves $324 on flights and $64.20 on the car, but its oceanfront room costs $445.28 more after tax. At Hanalei Shore, the later week is $223.28 less overall because the air and car savings exceed the higher room cost.
Compare the two later-week resorts beyond price. We would rather settle on a week first, and June 10 is looking more practical despite the limited oceanfront stock.

For June 10-17, Koloa Bay is $363.99 less in the complete trip comparison and keeps breakfast and parking inside the room total. Its available room is directly oceanfront with a balcony, king bed, mini-fridge, and in-room coffee. Hanalei Shore's available king is labeled deluxe ocean view rather than oceanfront; it also has a balcony and mini-fridge, but breakfast and parking remain separate. Hanalei Shore has the quieter north-shore setting, while Koloa Bay gives simpler access from LIH and a shorter transfer after the noon arrival.
How much driving should we expect on arrival and departure? We will pick up and return the car at LIH.

Under ordinary traffic, LIH to Koloa Bay is about 25-35 minutes, so a 12:04 p.m. arrival should put you at the resort around 1:30 after the rental pickup. LIH to Hanalei Shore is generally 50-65 minutes and can run longer with north-shore congestion, putting arrival closer to 2:00-2:20. For the 1:05 p.m. return flight, leaving Koloa Bay around 9:45 a.m. or Hanalei Shore around 9:10 a.m. allows time for fuel, car return, and airport processing.

Let's narrow it to June 10-17. I want one refundable plan at each resort so we can decide between them, but do not book anything yet. Confirm exactly what is refundable and whether the airfare is part of that.

For Koloa Bay, the $4,691.97 flexible hotel rate takes a one-night deposit but allows cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time on June 3 for a full deposit refund. For Hanalei Shore, the $5,055.96 flexible rate allows cancellation through 4:00 p.m. Hawaii time on June 5 without a hotel penalty; the card is held as a guarantee. The $548.20 car rate is pay later and can be canceled without charge before pickup. The quoted $566-per-person airfare is standard economy, not cash-refundable; cancellation would produce airline credit under the current fare rules. I have therefore left the flights, hotels, and car unbooked.

That is the right distinction. Keep both June 10 resort plans on the shortlist, using the same nonstop flights and the same full-stay car in the comparison. Note that the oceanfront room at Koloa Bay is the inventory risk, and leave the earlier week behind.

The vacation is narrowed to June 10-17, 2028. Plan A is Koloa Bay Resort in the oceanfront king at a complete estimated trip total of $6,372.17; its hotel deposit is fully refundable through 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time June 3, and the limited oceanfront inventory is the main availability risk. Plan B is Hanalei Shore Hotel in the deluxe ocean-view king at $6,736.16; its hotel rate is penalty-free through 4:00 p.m. Hawaii time June 5. Both use the 9:10 a.m. SFO-LIH nonstop, the 1:05 p.m. LIH-SFO return, and the $548.20 pay-later full-stay car. Nothing has been booked, and the June 3-10 week is no longer under consideration.
